classification.difficultyReason: Parts a and b are direct: 1/n, then multiply independent probabilities to get 1/(6n). The hardest part is c, which needs a representation change from the symbolic probability to an equation. The student sets 1/(6n) = 1/48 and solves for n, which is a short routine linked procedure with no interpretation or hidden insight. It is more demanding than the plain product-rule and listing tasks, which are single-step or enumeration work, because of the algebraic n and the reverse step. It is no harder than the multi-outcome spinner sums (p22-q14) or the algebraic-fraction modelling in A3.
